difficulty_reason: The author constructs anchored path witnesses in the random subdivision of a binary tree. The load-bearing step combines 2^n pairwise disjoint paths from level n to level 2n with the non-exponential tail of the subdivision lengths: the printed Comment obtains the bound 1-(1-exp(-epsilon*n))^(2^n) for finding a path of total length at least c*n. The selected path is extended to the root, and the printed boundary-to-subdivided-length ratio is at most (2*n+1)/(c*n), tending to 2/c; c is arbitrary. The non-routine content is the choice of exponentially many independent path candidates together with control of the boundary of an anchored witness, not a one-end boundary count or a union-bound description. The exercise on physical p.252 and the closing conclusion of its complete Comment on physical p.638 both use Phi*_E. Physical p.238 separately defines Phi**_E and states Phi**_E=Phi*_E for trees; there is no single-star/double-star discrepancy between this exercise and its Comment. The printed statements about infinitely many n and the almost-sure conclusion remain as the author wrote them, without adding a proof step. This is one H2 material judgment and not an independent certification of the mathematics.

statement_spans.source_role: Complete original Exercise6.88, the single counted target: for a binary tree G and a subdivision law nu whose tail decays slower than exponentially, Phi*_E(G) > 0 yet Phi*_E(G_nu) = 0 a.s., with G_nu the Section 6.9 random subdivision.

proof_spans.source_role: Original Exercise 6.88 with its complete printed author Comment on physical p. 638: the failure of an exponential tail gives P[sum_{i<=n} L_i >= cn] >= P[L_1 >= cn] >= e^{-eps n} for infinitely many n; the 2^n pairwise disjoint level-n-to-level-2n paths of the binary tree give, by union bound, 1 - (1-e^{-eps n})^{2^n} >= 1 - exp(-e^{-eps n} 2^n) -> 1; a good path extended to the root gives |d_E S| / sum_{e in E(S)} L_e <= (2n+1)/(cn) ~ 2/c; and since c is arbitrary the closing display asserts the vanishing of the anchored constant a.s. The uncounted context reprints the anchored constants of physical p. 234, the edge-set notation (6.33) of physical p. 217, the random-subdivision and exponential-tail definitions with Phi**_E and Theorem 6.50 on physical p. 238, and the necessity remark that cites the exercise on physical p. 240. No author step is expanded or repaired, no constant is synchronised and no hypothesis is altered.

source_roles.literal_source_feature: Measured, not inherited: the constant printed on physical p. 252 in the question and in the closing display of the Comment on physical p. 638 carries exactly one raised script-size asterisk at 6.30 pt per occurrence (p. 252: three occurrences, none with two; p. 638: one occurrence, none with two), while the double-star symbol occurs only on physical pp. 238 and 240, set as two raised asterisks at 7.35 pt, and the unanchored constant of Exercise 6.23 on physical p. 238 has no asterisk at all. The owner material review, the independent material review and the owner adjudication all describe the printed link between this exercise and the body as the inequality Phi**_E <= Phi*_E, which is a misreading of the double-star symbol; those three reports are left unedited and the measured reading is recorded here. The printed link that does close the Comment's last step is the tree equality Phi**_E(G) = Phi*_E(G) printed on physical p. 238, which the adjudication itself states. The Comment's denominators are kept as printed: L_e and sum_{e in E(S)} L_e over the edge set E(S), and partial_E S over the vertex set S.
